data.generation: Euler-Maruyama with dt = 0.001 for the nonlinear sigmoid drift (no exact transition exists); observations are every 0.05 on [0, 1] (21 points per trajectory). Data are regenerated here: the paper does not publish its generated dataset.
data.initial_law: X_0 ~ N(0, I_2) (declared cut: the paper's Section 6 does not state the initial law for the synthetic experiment; the DLGM definition in Section 2 sets X_0 = Z_0 ~ N(0, I), which is adopted here and recorded)
data.note: Paper Section 6: dX_t = sigmoid(A X_t) dt + dW_t on t in [0, 1], A in R^{d x d} drawn i.i.d. N(0, 1), observations Y_i = X_1 plus independent Gaussian noise of covariance I_d. The paper's experiment uses d = 10 (A 10 x 10, beta in R^10, n = 1000 for its Figure 1); this study cuts to d = 2 with n = 4096 trajectories (CPU cut, recorded as a deviation). The activation is read as the coordinatewise logistic sigmoid (the paper's Eq. (21) writes sigmoid(A X_t)); the ar5iv rendering's phrase 'sigmoid softplus' is ambiguous and is recorded as a reading risk in the report, not silently resolved.

distillation.library_variables: polynomials in (x1, x2) only: the paper's SDE is time-homogeneous, so no t variable enters the library (contrast with Day 2's (t, z) library)
distillation.oracle_diagnostic: the same SINDy procedure fitted to ground-truth field values at the same query states (diagnostic ceiling only, not a candidate)
distillation.query_states: observed states of each split (trajectory-disjoint train/validation/test), teacher evaluated directly (no finite differences)
distillation.selection: per field, minimize validation NRMSE against the teacher; test evaluated once after selection

ground_truth_sde.form: dX_t = sigmoid(A X_t) dt + dW_t, t in [0, 1], sigmoid coordinatewise logistic

H3_truth_recovery.note: Verdict rests on the field clause plus the parametric teacher's coefficient clause (relative Frobenius error of A_hat vs A). Symbolic polynomial coefficients are NOT read as A: a polynomial is not the sigmoid, so its coefficients have no A interpretation; the train-query VIF is still reported, and if VIF > 10 no symbolic coefficient is interpreted at all (Day 2 reflection).

H5_estimator_bias.note: Day 1 reflection applied: discretization-bias diagnostic split by regime. Regimes are defined by the ground-truth linear predictor u = A x at the transition start: near-linear max|u| < 0.5, saturated max|u| > 1.5 (intermediate otherwise). The global g comparison is the verdict clause; the per-regime drift NRMSE (fitted teacher drift vs truth drift at test transition starts) is the diagnostic showing where any bias concentrates. Drift ordering is read together with field NRMSE, not from NLL ordering alone (Day 2 reflection: NLL differences at the 1e-5 scale are not systematic orderings).

H6_variational_mesh.note: Paper Section 6 claim, quantified here: improvements from meshes finer than h = 1/32 are incremental. Test: |F(h = 1/64) - F(h = 1/32)| <= 0.05 on validation terminal observations, free energy excluding the constant (d/2) log(2 pi), per observation, with the fitted shared-beta variational model. Finer mesh is computed by re-simulating the same fitted model at the finer step (no refit).

paper.experiment: Section 6: synthetic data from dX_t = sigmoid(A X_t) dt + dW_t, variational inference with a constant-shift (Girsanov mean-shift) approximate posterior, free energy vs discretization mesh and sample size
paper.title: Neural Stochastic Differential Equations: Deep Latent Gaussian Models in the Diffusion Limit

reflections_applied.day1_discretization_bias: Four Gaussian transition-likelihood estimators (EM / local linearization / local-linearization-exponential / substep moments) are compared on g and on drift NRMSE vs truth, with the comparison split by near-linear vs saturated regimes (the analogue of Day 1's linear-vs-nonlinear component split for a sigmoid drift). The distilled teacher is fixed a priori to the substep estimator (v4) because the absolute diffusion level is a primary question.
reflections_applied.day2_nll_sensitivity: Estimator drift ordering is judged by field NRMSE, not by validation NLL ordering; NLL differences are reported but not over-read.
reflections_applied.day2_off_manifold: Off-manifold grid diagnosis is standard: x1, x2 in {-3, -1.5, 0, 1.5, 3} (25 points), symbolic / teacher / truth compared on drift NRMSE, reported on three axes (field, coefficient, off-manifold) separately.
reflections_applied.day2_vif_gate: Train-query VIF(x1, x2) and degree-2 feature correlations are computed before fitting; with VIF > 10 no symbolic coefficient is interpreted.

teacher.architecture: Parametric neural SDE in the paper's own family: drift = sigmoid(A x) with trainable A in R^{2 x 2} (one linear layer + logistic sigmoid) and scalar diffusion g shared across coordinates. This is NOT a generic MLP: the paper's model class is exactly this single-layer form, and keeping it makes the teacher's coefficients (A) identifiable and comparable with the truth. The generic-MLP teacher of Days 1-2 is deliberately not used.
teacher.deviation_from_paper: Two declared cuts. (1) Dimension and sample size: d = 2, n = 4096 trajectories instead of d = 10, n = 1000. (2) The paper's variational inference is implemented only in its shared-beta form: one constant shift beta in R^2, shared across observations, optimized on train terminal observations with the Girsanov KL term 0.5 * ||beta||^2 (integral over [0, 1]) plus the Gaussian terminal reconstruction term. A per-observation amortized encoder beta(y) is out of scope for one CPU day, as is the paper's forward-mode pathwise differentiation (stochastic flows); the variational fit here uses discretize-then-differentiate Euler simulation with Adam, which the paper's Section 5.2 shows recovers stochastic backpropagation for the Euler scheme. The likelihood teachers (v1-v4) are diagnostic comparators in the series' style, not the paper's estimator; the distilled teacher is v4, fixed a priori. The paper's mesh/sample-size figures are re-tested only on the mesh axis (H6); the sample-size axis is not re-tested.
teacher.estimator: substep_moments (the distilled teacher, chosen A PRIORI per the Day 1 reflection)

estimators_compared.em: v1 plain Euler-Maruyama Gaussian transition likelihood over dt_obs = 0.05: mean x + f*dt, covariance g^2*dt*I
estimators_compared.local_linearization: v2 truncated local linearization: mean x + f*dt + 0.5*dt^2*J*f, covariance g^2*dt*I + g^2*dt^2*sym(J), symmetrized and eigenvalue-floored at 1e-8; J = diag(sigmoid'(A x)) A, treated as a fixed local coefficient (no_grad, analytic)
estimators_compared.local_linearization_exp: v3 matrix-exponential resummation with coefficients frozen at the step start: mean x + Psi*f with Psi = (expm(J*dt) - I) J^{-1} (pseudo-inverse fallback), covariance g^2 * integral_0^dt expm(J s) expm(J s)^T ds approximated by 8-point Gauss-Legendre quadrature (documented approximation)
estimators_compared.substep_moments: v4 simulation-based moment propagation with K = 8 internal substeps per observation interval: mean advanced by f at the current mean, covariance by V <- V + (J V + V J^T + g^2 I) h, J analytic at the current mean and treated as a fixed local coefficient; the Gaussian NLL is evaluated at the observed endpoint under the propagated (mean, covariance)

teacher.optimizer: Adam lr 0.01, checkpoint = min validation transition NLL (likelihood teachers) / min validation free energy (variational fit)

variational.free_energy: per observation, constant-excluded: F = E_paths[0.5 * ||beta||^2 + 0.5 * ||Y - X_1||^2]; the reported F adds (d/2) log(2 pi) back as F_reported. The KL term uses the Girsanov form for a constant shift with unit diffusion: 0.5 * integral_0^1 ||beta||^2 dt = 0.5 * ||beta||^2.
variational.mesh_study: fitted variational model re-simulated at h in {1/8, 1/16, 1/32, 1/64} on validation terminal observations, 4096 paths per mesh, seed 7
